title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's high-performance computing (HPC) environment. Kobalos is a sophisticated backdoor malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems. It provides remote access, terminal session capabilities, and credential stealing functionality. Your mission is to investigate the compromised systems, identify the malware's persistence mechanisms, and contain the threat. You will need to find specific service names, persistence mechanisms, and lateral movement artifacts as part of your investigation.
outcomes: Usage of systemctl for service discovery
Usage of journalctl for service logs
Investigation of systemd timers for persistence

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's high-performance computing (HPC) environment. Kobalos is a sophisticated backdoor malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems. It provides remote access, terminal session capabilities, and credential stealing functionality.

Your mission is to investigate the compromised systems, identify the malware's persistence mechanisms, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring your organization's HPC environment, you noticed unusual network traffic originating from the target host. Your first task is to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on this host that might be responsible for this activity. The flag you are looking for is the name of the suspicious service (a string).

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Use standard Linux commands to list running services and check their legitimacy.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for any services that are not part of the standard system configuration or that have unusual properties.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check for services that might be related to the Kobalos malware.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you've identified a suspicious service, you need to determine how it maintains persistence on the system. Investigate the system's startup mechanisms to find out how the service is automatically started after reboot. The flag you are looking for is the name of the persistence mechanism (a string).

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for timers that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check for any unusual entries in the systemd timer files.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Your investigation has revealed that the malware might be attempting to move laterally within your network. Examine the system for evidence of file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts. Focus on any connections to the next-target host (IP: 192.168.50.6). The flag you are looking for is the name of the target host (a string).

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for scripts or binaries related to file transfers.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check the logs of any services that might be involved in lateral movement.
